newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Solothurner Bank complaint names Arthur Andersen.
newsitem.headline: Solothurner Bank complaint names Arthur Andersen.

text.p: Swiss regional bank Solothurner Bank said filed a complaint involving 144 million Swiss francs in damages against the Zurich office of international auditing and consulting concern Arthur Andersen.
The complaint was filed in the Zurich Court of Commerce in early March.
Arthur Andersen, in a separate statement, said that it rejected the accusations.
The plaintiffs allege the auditing firm took improper care in its role in a takeover by Solothurner Cantonalbank of another bank, Bank in Kriegstetten, finalised in 1993.

"After the acquisition it was found that the value assessed by Arthur Andersen did not match the effective value of the Bank in Kriegstetten and millions were needed for additional provisions," the Solothurner Bank said.
"Arthur Andersen has taken note of Solothurner Bank's complaint. The complaint contains no new elements," it said.

It said further that Solothurner Cantonalbank reached a decision to purchase Bank in Kriegstetten on May 16, 1992. Further, it said that its contract was at first limited to a "summary computation of value."
"The work did not include in any way or form a comprehensive evaluation, let alone a full audit," it said.

Both banks hired Arthur Andersen on May 18, 1992 to evaluate the Bank in Kriegstetten as per June 30, 1992, in view of Solothurner Cantonalbank's plans to acquire the rest of its shares, after Solothurner Cantonalbank took over roughly 35 percent of Bank in Kriegstetten's shares.

Arthur Andersen produced a share valuation of 720 francs, compared with 1,200 francs made in an earlier assessment by another firm. In October 1992 Solothurner Cantonalbank made a takeover offer priced at 700 francs.
In November 1992 Arther Andersen was made auditor according to Swiss banking law of Bank in Kriegstetten, and in its new function discovered "grave problems" in its control systems.

"On September 6, 1993 Solothurner Cantonalbank decided to completely integrate Bank in Kriegstetten. With this merger, Solothurner Cantonalbank made Bank in Kriegstetten's problems its own. Based on these facts, Arthur Andersen regards the accusations raised as unfounded," Arthur Andersen said.
Solothurner Bank is a 100-percent subsidiary of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC). SBC referred queries to Solothurner Bank.
Solothurner Bank is the legal entity set up following the financial collapse of then-independent Solothurner Cantonalbank. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
